title: DBT Explained: What It Is and Who It Helps
description: Dialectical Behavior Therapy combines CBT with mindfulness. How it works, the four skill modules, who benefits most, and how to find DBT treatment.

content.text: DBT was created for people who feel emotions intensely and struggle with self-destructive behaviors. It's now used for a wide range of emotional difficulties. Here's how it works.
DBT is a type of CBT that adds two key elements:

items: Dialectics: Balancing acceptance AND change (you're doing your best AND you need to change)
Mindfulness: Present-moment awareness as a core skill

content.text: This makes it particularly effective for people who feel invalidated by pure change-focused therapy.
The foundation. Learning to observe your thoughts and feelings without judgment, staying present rather than reacting impulsively.
Surviving crisis without making things worse. Skills like TIPP (Temperature, Intense exercise, Paced breathing, Progressive relaxation) for immediate relief.
Understanding and managing emotions. Identifying triggers, increasing positive experiences, reducing emotional vulnerability.
Asking for what you need, saying no, maintaining relationships and self-respect. Specific scripts like DEAR MAN for difficult conversations.
Full DBT is intensive. For less severe presentations, 'DBT-informed' therapy or skills-only groups may be appropriate—but for BPD and severe emotion dysregulation, full DBT is most effective.

items: Ask: 'Do you provide all four modes of DBT?'
University-based clinics often have DBT programs

content.text: DBT is a comprehensive treatment for people who struggle with intense emotions and self-destructive behaviors. It combines practical skills with acceptance. If emotions feel overwhelming and you've struggled with other treatments, DBT may be worth exploring.
